entries.headline: KubeCoderConfig jenkins-pipelines skill: its FILE-1 and LIB-2 lines will contradict the guide once the one-call producer exception lands
body: The skill (`kubecoder/skills/jenkins-pipelines/SKILL.md`, read on gitblit `main`) summarises FILE-1 as "One declarative `pipeline {}`; no scripted `node`, `podTemplate` or `stage` outside it" (lines 35-36). It summarises LIB-2 as "The library never takes over the job's properties, trigger or agent size" (lines 151-152). Slice 035's P1 amends both rules in the guide with Ruling D2's exception for a type with a whole-pipeline helper, and 75 producers become one `architectureProducer` call. No phase targets KubeCoderConfig, because the plan keeps to the repos the refinement named, so the skill's summaries stay as they are. 034's close-out I1 already notes that nothing keeps the skill's summaries in step with the guide.
entries.consequence: A session that reviews or edits a producer from the skill's summaries flags a one-call Jenkinsfile.architecture as breaking FILE-1 and LIB-2 until it reads the guide's page.
entries.author: plan-writer, planning r1, KubeCoderConfig kubecoder/skills/jenkins-pipelines/SKILL.md (gitblit main)

The skill's library section (KubeCoderConfig kubecoder/skills/jenkins-pipelines/SKILL.md:147-159, gitblit main) does not mention J16's status.

entries.headline: Architecture producer manual: § Jenkins integration still shows a scripted podTemplate producer, not the guide's form or the architectureProducer helper
body: `.claude/architecture/producer-manual.md` § Jenkins integration (around lines 690-720) gives a scripted `podTemplate`/`node` snippet with `containerTemplates.aac_tools`, followed by separate validate and archive steps, and `:659` points there. The seed-architecture skill (`.claude/skills/seed-architecture/SKILL.md:147-150`) also sends a new producer to `containerTemplates.aac_tools`. Since 034 the style guide has been the source of a Jenkinsfile's form. After 035, each architecture type's reference is a one-call `architectureProducer` file. No phase of this slice targets Architecture. Once the second slice retires the containerTemplates describables (033 I1), the snippet stops working altogether.
entries.consequence: A session that seeds a new producer from the manual writes a scripted producer that the style guide rejects, until the jenkins-pipelines skill or a review corrects it.
entries.author: plan-writer, planning r1, Architecture .claude/architecture/producer-manual.md

text: Under Ruling D2 as reversed at plan review r1, each architecture type's reference after 035 is a full declarative file whose stages call architectureProducer's steps. It is not a one-call file. The manual's gap is the same, measured against that file instead.

entries.headline: Ansible argo-migrate: scaffold and add_stage still write the scripted, hand-cloning Jenkinsfile.architecture
body: `support/argo-migrate/argo_migrate.py:192-221` (`JENKINSFILE_ARCH`) templates a deploy repo's producer as `podTemplate`/`node` with `git branch: 'main', credentialsId:`. `cmd_scaffold` (`:1123`) and `add_stage` (`:946`) write it. Once 035 lands, every deploy-repo producer is one `architectureProducer` call, and this template is the only source left that writes the old form. Both commands read HelmCharts, which is archived, so a run is possible only for the parked apps. The plan leaves the template alone because it is not a producer.
entries.consequence: A deploy repo scaffolded for one of the parked apps gets a producer in the old scripted form with a hand clone, outside the style guide, and that producer stops working once the second slice retires the containerTemplates describables.

entries.headline: Settle V14 after the operator's next KubeCoder promotion (KubeCoder/Promote-PRD), which …
body: V14 — AaC/KubeCoderDeploy builds its migrated file green from `prd`. The slice commits that file on KubeCoderDeploy's `main`. The job builds `prd`, which only KubeCoder/Promote-PRD fast-forwards (`JenkinsPipelineUtils/docs/pages/guide/job-properties.md:53`), so the push starts no build of it.

`verification.json` marks V14 owed after: the operator's next KubeCoder promotion (KubeCoder/Promote-PRD), which fast-forwards KubeCoderDeploy's prd to main. The run cannot take that action; settle the criterion once it has happened.
entries.consequence: V14 stays unproven until then; the test phase does not settle it.
entries.author: `verification.json`'s `owed_after`, seeded by the plan loop

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils architectureProducer.archive: its collector check accepts a comma-joined entry, so an uncollected pattern can slip past it
body: `collected()` splits an entry on `/` only (`vars/architectureProducer.groovy:88-90`). `archivePattern` joins the entries with `,` (`:80`), and `archiveArtifacts` splits on commas. So `files: ['docs/architecture/a.yaml,*/architecture.yaml']` passes the check, and `*/architecture.yaml` is archived where AaC/Architecture never looks. That is the DockerImages case the check exists to refuse (`vars/architectureProducer.md:80-81`). No producer calls the step that way yet. ElectronicsInventory's current archive is one comma-joined string (`Jenkinsfile.architecture:39`), so a hand copy could produce such an entry, but both of its halves are collected.
entries.consequence: A producer that passes a comma-joined entry can archive a model the collector never collects, and nothing refuses it.
entries.author: code-reviewer, P1, round 1, phases/P1/code_review_r1.md F1

entries.headline: JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/architectureProducer.md: 'A pattern that matches no file fails the build' is false for a files list with several entries
body: `vars/architectureProducer.md:82` says an archive pattern that matches no file fails the build. `archiveArtifacts` puts every pattern into one Ant FileSet and aborts only when the whole set is empty (Jenkins core `ArtifactArchiver.perform`). So one empty entry among several is skipped without a word. The sentence holds only when no entry matches any file: that restriction is the one-edit fix. In the plan's shapes `validate` runs first on the same files and fails on an unmatched glob, so nothing goes wrong today.
entries.consequence: A producer author who relies on archive to catch a missing model, with several entries, gets a green build that archives only part of the model.
entries.author: code-reviewer, P1, round 1, phases/P1/code_review_r1.md F2

entries.headline: AnsibleSpecs review report.md J16 note: says each producer is about 40 lines; 50 of the 78 are 62 lines or more
body: reviews/2026-09-jenkinsfile-review/report.md:807-809 (J16's Delivered note, added in P5) reads 'Each producer stays a full declarative file of about 40 lines: header, library line, and pipeline {} ... The operator accepted that length.' The committed files are 47 lines (single-model app files, Ansible), 59 (the three monorepos, DockerImages), 62 (48 deploy files), 69/70 (ArgoCDDeploy, KubeCoderDeploy) and 93 (IoTSupport). The ~40 figure is Ruling D2's estimate (plan.md:91), and the note restates it as the files' measured length.
entries.consequence: A reader of the review's record takes the producers to be about 40 lines long, when most are 62 lines or more.

entries.headline: Run stopped (protocol_failure) in P5
body: The driver's bail (`protocol_failure`), as it recorded it:

> the driver's own run record was committed onto phase/035-P5 (a `git add -A` in /work/AnsibleSpecs): slices/035_architecture_producers_declarative/phases/P5/code_review_r1.md, slices/035_architecture_producers_declarative/phases/P5/review_result_r1.json. Rewrite the branch without those paths, then resume.
entries.consequence: none the loop acts on — what the stop needed was settled outside the run before it resumed where it stopped; recorded so the report accounts for every stop the run header counts.

entries.headline: Run stopped (lost_work) in P5
body: The driver's bail (`lost_work`), as it recorded it:

> commit 638d9cbe3a39 is on P5's record as work the driver saw on the branch, and phase/035-P5 in /work/AnsibleSpecs does not carry it. Something rebuilt the branch or replaced the checkout under the run; the loop will not carry on over the top of a commit it cannot account for. Check that no second driver is on this slice (each holds run.lock), then either restore the branch or clear the phase's record in state.json (status, stage, gate_green_commit, reviewed_head) to run it again from the executor.
entries.consequence: none the loop acts on — what the stop needed was settled outside the run before it resumed where it stopped; recorded so the report accounts for every stop the run header counts.
